bull_bear.body:
- First-mover heritage: promoted by Mr. Ashok Jaipuria, a first-generation entrepreneur described as having introduced the country to soft ferrite cores; company established in 1986
- In-house developed technology - the AR states the Company's technology is developed in-house, with no technology imported in the last three years, yielding product improvement, process enhancement, cost reduction and import substitution
- In-house R&D resource centre equipped with XRF, XRD, computerised BET surface analyser, 1000x digital microscope, particle size analyser, atmosphere-controlled lab-scale sintering kiln, precision impedance analyser (to 5 MHz) and a power-loss / B-H loop tracer (to 2 MHz)
- Broad product catalogue across core geometries with wide size ranges (e.g. EE cores 10-128 mm, toroids 6-202 mm, planar cores 18-153 mm), supporting diversified end-use applications
- Natural hedge on foreign exchange - being both an importer and an exporter, currency risk is partially mitigated
- Quality and compliance accreditations (ISO 9001/14001, ISO/TS 16949, RoHS, REACH, UL insulation coating) relevant to automotive and power-electronics customers
- Stated mitigation of competition through exports presence, niche value-added products and new market/customer development; management states the domestic market caters to the lower end of the ferrites market and poses no threat, and that the company has a good image with local customers
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material price volatility — The industry is dependent on key raw materials such as iron oxide, manganese oxide, zinc oxide, nickel oxide and copper; management states that fluctuations in commodity prices, supply disruptions or geopolitical developments may affect production costs and margins. Cosmo Ferrites converts purchased oxides into ferrite powder and cores, so input cost is the dominant swing factor on an already thin margin.
- Competition and pricing pressure in standardised products — Management states the market is characterised by competition from both global and regional manufacturers and that sustained pricing pressure, particularly in standardized product categories, may impact profitability and market share. Mitigation is stated as increasing export presence, developing niche products and exploring new markets and customers; management adds that the domestic market caters to the lower end of the ferrites market and poses no threat to the company.
- Customer attrition / concentration on quality, delivery and price — Management flags that all customers are sensitive to quality, delivery and price, mitigated by value-added niche products, customer schedule adherence and improved quality standards. As a component supplier into automotive, EV and power-electronics OEMs, losing a qualified customer is slow to replace.
- Technological obsolescence in a fast-moving product cycle — The MD&A states the industry faces the challenge of rapid technological advancements and that companies unable to continuously innovate and upgrade their manufacturing processes and product capabilities may face risks of obsolescence and loss of market share. The stated demand shift toward wide-bandgap semiconductors, higher switching frequencies and advanced EMI management raises the technical bar for ferrite materials.
- Quality and reliability requirements in safety-critical applications — Ferrite cores are described as critical components in power conversion and energy management systems, so maintaining stringent quality standards and product reliability is stated to be essential to sustain customer relationships and meet regulatory and industry specifications.
- Export demand, trade and currency exposure — Management states that uncertainties in global trade environments, including sanctions, currency volatility and regional economic slowdowns, may affect export demand and pricing competitiveness. Separately, the Company is exposed to foreign exchange risk mainly due to imported raw materials and finished products, though being both importer and exporter the currency risk is partially mitigated through a natural hedge.
- Energy, freight and logistics cost escalation from geopolitical conflict — Geopolitical conflicts have introduced volatility in the supply of key raw materials and logistics networks, leading to potential disruptions and cost escalations, and fluctuations in energy prices and freight costs may adversely impact operating margins. Energy is a material line for a kiln-based sintering process.
- Operational disruption at a single manufacturing location — Under Security Risk Management the Company states that operations could be disrupted due to natural, political and economic disturbances; it has taken insurance cover on insurable interests (fire, marine, burglary, group personal accident and other miscellaneous policies) and has strengthened IT and physical security systems at all locations. The Board separately states there are no risks which in its opinion threaten the existence of the Company.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Cosmo Ferrites manufactures Mn-Zn based soft ferrite cores and pre-calcined ferrite powder. Its cores are used in inverter transformers, EV chargers, energy meters, mobile chargers, SMPS, pulse transformers, line filters, chokes and noise suppressors. The company describes itself as dealing in Soft Ferrites Core and Transformer, selling roughly 73% into the domestic Indian market and 27% into exports.

outlook.body:
- Develop new markets in the global arena while focusing on cost cutting and increased productivity to enhance competitiveness (stated Outlook).
- Leverage technological capabilities, expand customer relationships and optimise manufacturing capacities to capitalise on emerging opportunities across key growth sectors.
- Move up the value chain into advanced powder solutions with lower power loss, higher saturation flux density, enhanced permeability and improved frequency response, targeted at EVs, automotive, telecommunications and solar energy.
- Counter competitive pricing pressure by increasing export presence, developing niche and value-added products, and exploring new markets and new customers.
- Mitigate customer attrition through value-added niche products, customer schedule adherence and improved quality standards, building long-term customer relationships.
- Rely on in-house developed technology rather than imported technology, targeting product improvement, process enhancement, cost reduction, product development and import substitution; new verticals created in NiZn products and new products for solar inverters, space vehicles and automotive applications.
- Continuous R&D effort explicitly directed at expanding both domestic and export markets.
- Continue energy-efficiency and alternate-energy initiatives (contract demand revision, solar generation, efficient air compressors, motion sensors) as a cost lever.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The routed bundle discloses no new plant, greenfield project or dated capacity-addition programme. Cosmo Ferrites operates a single manufacturing facility located in the foothills of the Himalayas at Jabli, Solan District, Himachal Pradesh, whose kiln line comprises five pusher kilns and one batch kiln with a total installed capacity of 3,900 tonnes per annum. Expansion during FY26 was expressed as better use of the existing asset base rather than new capital projects: management states that growth was supported by improved capacity utilization and a strategic expansion of the customer base across domestic and international markets, and that the Company remains focused on leveraging its technological capabilities, expanding customer relationships and optimizing manufacturing capacities to capitalize on emerging opportunities across key growth sectors. Product-side expansion took the form of the successful development and commercialization of advanced powder solutions for EVs, automotive, telecommunications and solar energy. No commissioning, ramp-up or debottlenecking timeline, and no rupee capex quantum, is stated anywhere in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The soft ferrite industry is experiencing steady growth and is expected to expand at an accelerated pace in coming years in both domestic and export markets, driven by rapid urbanisation and increasing adoption of electronic and power management devices.
- Increasing adoption of the Company's products in the EV and solar segments contributed significantly to business momentum, supported by the global transition towards clean energy and sustainable mobility.
- Growth during the year was supported by improved capacity utilisation and strategic expansion of the customer base across domestic and international markets; continued penetration into export markets and diversified end-use applications strengthened market position.
- FY26 performance improvement was driven by higher sales volumes, improved average realizations, and market expansions.
- Geopolitical focus on defence preparedness is raising demand for advanced electronic systems (communication equipment, radar, power electronics) in which soft ferrite cores are integral, creating incremental demand opportunities.
- Increased investments in energy security - renewable energy systems, grid infrastructure and backup power - are expected to drive demand for transformers, inverters and SMPS, supporting soft ferrite growth.
- Localization of manufacturing in electric vehicles and consumer electronics augurs well for domestic demand.
- Industry estimates cited by management indicate the global power transformer market is projected to grow at a CAGR of approximately 6-7% over the next five to seven years, with Asia-Pacific the fastest-growing region.
- The transition toward wide-bandgap semiconductors, higher switching frequencies, compact power conversion systems and advanced EMI management is driving demand for ferrite materials with superior permeability, lower core losses and enhanced frequency response.
- Growth in EVs, renewable energy systems, telecommunications infrastructure and data centers is expected to remain a key demand catalyst for advanced ferrite products; rising transformer demand from data centers, EV charging networks and renewable projects has created supply-demand imbalances in several markets.
- Margin watch-items: volatility in raw material supply and logistics from geopolitical conflict, and fluctuations in energy prices and freight costs, may adversely impact operating margins; sanctions, currency volatility and regional slowdowns may affect export demand and pricing competitiveness.
- Overall impact of geopolitical tension on the soft ferrite cores industry is expected to remain balanced with a positive medium- to long-term outlook, subject to companies' ability to adapt to evolving market dynamics and technological requirements.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The soft ferrite industry is experiencing steady growth and is expected to expand at an accelerated pace in coming years in both domestic and export markets, driven by rapid urbanisation and increasing adoption of electronic and power management devices.
- Increasing adoption of the Company's products in the EV and solar segments contributed significantly to business momentum, supported by the global transition towards clean energy and sustainable mobility.
- Growth during the year was supported by improved capacity utilisation and strategic expansion of the customer base across domestic and international markets; continued penetration into export markets and diversified end-use applications strengthened market position.
- FY26 performance improvement was driven by higher sales volumes, improved average realizations, and market expansions.
- Geopolitical focus on defence preparedness is raising demand for advanced electronic systems (communication equipment, radar, power electronics) in which soft ferrite cores are integral, creating incremental demand opportunities.
- Increased investments in energy security - renewable energy systems, grid infrastructure and backup power - are expected to drive demand for transformers, inverters and SMPS, supporting soft ferrite growth.
- Localization of manufacturing in electric vehicles and consumer electronics augurs well for domestic demand.
- Industry estimates cited by management indicate the global power transformer market is projected to grow at a CAGR of approximately 6-7% over the next five to seven years, with Asia-Pacific the fastest-growing region.
- The transition toward wide-bandgap semiconductors, higher switching frequencies, compact power conversion systems and advanced EMI management is driving demand for ferrite materials with superior permeability, lower core losses and enhanced frequency response.
- Growth in EVs, renewable energy systems, telecommunications infrastructure and data centers is expected to remain a key demand catalyst for advanced ferrite products; rising transformer demand from data centers, EV charging networks and renewable projects has created supply-demand imbalances in several markets.
- Margin watch-items: volatility in raw material supply and logistics from geopolitical conflict, and fluctuations in energy prices and freight costs, may adversely impact operating margins; sanctions, currency volatility and regional slowdowns may affect export demand and pricing competitiveness.
- Overall impact of geopolitical tension on the soft ferrite cores industry is expected to remain balanced with a positive medium- to long-term outlook, subject to companies' ability to adapt to evolving market dynamics and technological requirements.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Develop new markets in the global arena while focusing on cost cutting and increased productivity to enhance competitiveness (stated Outlook).
- Leverage technological capabilities, expand customer relationships and optimise manufacturing capacities to capitalise on emerging opportunities across key growth sectors.
- Move up the value chain into advanced powder solutions with lower power loss, higher saturation flux density, enhanced permeability and improved frequency response, targeted at EVs, automotive, telecommunications and solar energy.
- Counter competitive pricing pressure by increasing export presence, developing niche and value-added products, and exploring new markets and new customers.
- Mitigate customer attrition through value-added niche products, customer schedule adherence and improved quality standards, building long-term customer relationships.
- Rely on in-house developed technology rather than imported technology, targeting product improvement, process enhancement, cost reduction, product development and import substitution; new verticals created in NiZn products and new products for solar inverters, space vehicles and automotive applications.
- Continuous R&D effort explicitly directed at expanding both domestic and export markets.
- Continue energy-efficiency and alternate-energy initiatives (contract demand revision, solar generation, efficient air compressors, motion sensors) as a cost lever.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The routed bundle discloses no new plant, greenfield project or dated capacity-addition programme. Cosmo Ferrites operates a single manufacturing facility located in the foothills of the Himalayas at Jabli, Solan District, Himachal Pradesh, whose kiln line comprises five pusher kilns and one batch kiln with a total installed capacity of 3,900 tonnes per annum. Expansion during FY26 was expressed as better use of the existing asset base rather than new capital projects: management states that growth was supported by improved capacity utilization and a strategic expansion of the customer base across domestic and international markets, and that the Company remains focused on leveraging its technological capabilities, expanding customer relationships and optimizing manufacturing capacities to capitalize on emerging opportunities across key growth sectors. Product-side expansion took the form of the successful development and commercialization of advanced powder solutions for EVs, automotive, telecommunications and solar energy. No commissioning, ramp-up or debottlenecking timeline, and no rupee capex quantum, is stated anywhere in this bundle.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- First-mover heritage: promoted by Mr. Ashok Jaipuria, a first-generation entrepreneur described as having introduced the country to soft ferrite cores; company established in 1986
- In-house developed technology - the AR states the Company's technology is developed in-house, with no technology imported in the last three years, yielding product improvement, process enhancement, cost reduction and import substitution
- In-house R&D resource centre equipped with XRF, XRD, computerised BET surface analyser, 1000x digital microscope, particle size analyser, atmosphere-controlled lab-scale sintering kiln, precision impedance analyser (to 5 MHz) and a power-loss / B-H loop tracer (to 2 MHz)
- Broad product catalogue across core geometries with wide size ranges (e.g. EE cores 10-128 mm, toroids 6-202 mm, planar cores 18-153 mm), supporting diversified end-use applications
- Natural hedge on foreign exchange - being both an importer and an exporter, currency risk is partially mitigated
- Quality and compliance accreditations (ISO 9001/14001, ISO/TS 16949, RoHS, REACH, UL insulation coating) relevant to automotive and power-electronics customers
- Stated mitigation of competition through exports presence, niche value-added products and new market/customer development; management states the domestic market caters to the lower end of the ferrites market and poses no threat, and that the company has a good image with local customers

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Raw material price volatility — The industry is dependent on key raw materials such as iron oxide, manganese oxide, zinc oxide, nickel oxide and copper; management states that fluctuations in commodity prices, supply disruptions or geopolitical developments may affect production costs and margins. Cosmo Ferrites converts purchased oxides into ferrite powder and cores, so input cost is the dominant swing factor on an already thin margin.
- Competition and pricing pressure in standardised products — Management states the market is characterised by competition from both global and regional manufacturers and that sustained pricing pressure, particularly in standardized product categories, may impact profitability and market share. Mitigation is stated as increasing export presence, developing niche products and exploring new markets and customers; management adds that the domestic market caters to the lower end of the ferrites market and poses no threat to the company.
- Customer attrition / concentration on quality, delivery and price — Management flags that all customers are sensitive to quality, delivery and price, mitigated by value-added niche products, customer schedule adherence and improved quality standards. As a component supplier into automotive, EV and power-electronics OEMs, losing a qualified customer is slow to replace.
- Technological obsolescence in a fast-moving product cycle — The MD&A states the industry faces the challenge of rapid technological advancements and that companies unable to continuously innovate and upgrade their manufacturing processes and product capabilities may face risks of obsolescence and loss of market share. The stated demand shift toward wide-bandgap semiconductors, higher switching frequencies and advanced EMI management raises the technical bar for ferrite materials.
- Quality and reliability requirements in safety-critical applications — Ferrite cores are described as critical components in power conversion and energy management systems, so maintaining stringent quality standards and product reliability is stated to be essential to sustain customer relationships and meet regulatory and industry specifications.
- Export demand, trade and currency exposure — Management states that uncertainties in global trade environments, including sanctions, currency volatility and regional economic slowdowns, may affect export demand and pricing competitiveness. Separately, the Company is exposed to foreign exchange risk mainly due to imported raw materials and finished products, though being both importer and exporter the currency risk is partially mitigated through a natural hedge.
- Energy, freight and logistics cost escalation from geopolitical conflict — Geopolitical conflicts have introduced volatility in the supply of key raw materials and logistics networks, leading to potential disruptions and cost escalations, and fluctuations in energy prices and freight costs may adversely impact operating margins. Energy is a material line for a kiln-based sintering process.
- Operational disruption at a single manufacturing location — Under Security Risk Management the Company states that operations could be disrupted due to natural, political and economic disturbances; it has taken insurance cover on insurable interests (fire, marine, burglary, group personal accident and other miscellaneous policies) and has strengthened IT and physical security systems at all locations. The Board separately states there are no risks which in its opinion threaten the existence of the Company.
